clue.text: Position of the King at Agincourt

definitions.text: Position of the King at Agincourt

parts.words: Position of the King at Agincourt
parts.note: the English king who won at Agincourt was Henry, and his place in the line of Henrys is the ordinal wanted

explanation.surface: A question about where the monarch stood on the battlefield in 1415.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Position' suggests a spot on the field, but it means rank in a numbered sequence: Henry V led the English at Agincourt.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry V was the king at Agincourt, so his numbered place among the Henrys is the ordinal after fourth.

clue.text: Being born on Monday is so attractive

definitions.text: Being born on Monday is so attractive

parts.words: Being born on Monday is so attractive
parts.note: the nursery rhyme says Monday's child is fair of face, so a Monday baby has a pretty face

explanation.surface: A claim that babies born on Mondays are good-looking.
explanation.walkthrough: The rhyme 'Monday's child is fair of face' gives the compound for having a pleasing look.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a fair or pleasing face means being attractive to look at.

clue.text: Initial honours degree

definitions.meaning: the top class of British university honours degree

explanation.surface: A student's initial top-class university result.
explanation.definitionFit: Earliest in order, and the top class of British university degree, share one word.

clue.text: Three men dismissed in succession during overtime?

definitions.text: Three men dismissed in succession during overtime?

parts.words: Three men dismissed in succession during overtime?
parts.note: the picture is of sackings from a workplace, but it is the cricket feat of taking three wickets with consecutive balls

explanation.surface: A firm sacking three workers one after another during extra hours.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a bowler who dismisses three batsmen with successive balls takes this; 'overtime' plays on the overs bowled.
explanation.definitionFit: Three batsmen out to consecutive deliveries is the cricket feat named this, also used for three goals by one player.

clue.text: 'You come most upon your hour' (Hamlet)

parts.note: the opening scene of Hamlet has Barnardo greeted with this line, with one adverb dropped out of the quotation

explanation.surface: A line quoted from the opening scene of Shakespeare's Hamlet, with a word gone.
explanation.walkthrough: The full line, said by Francisco to Barnardo on the battlements, is 'You come most carefully upon your hour'; the missing adverb is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The gap in the Shakespeare quotation is filled by the adverb meaning punctually and with caution.

clue.text: Pretty clever

explanation.surface: Fairly smart, or a compliment that is quite clever.
explanation.definitionFit: Charmingly attractive and shrewdly sharp are both senses of this word.

clue.text: Vigorous Marxist initiated

parts.note: red is a familiar label for a communist or Marxist
someone blooded has been initiated, given a first taste of action

explanation.surface: An energetic communist inducted into the movement.
explanation.definitionFit: Full of vitality and manly energy is the sense of this hyphenated word.

clue.text: Flaws in the service

parts.note: the service seems to be a church or military one, but it is a tennis serve, where bad serves are called by this name

explanation.surface: Things going wrong during a church service or in the armed forces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'service' suggests church or the forces; in tennis an illegal serve is called this.
explanation.definitionFit: Defects in general, and illegal serves in tennis, share this word.

clue.text: Persistent theme — limit vote fixing?

indicators.note: a fixed vote is one rigged, so the letters of the two words are rigged into a new order

explanation.surface: A recurring complaint about rigging a capped ballot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fixing' rearranges LIMIT VOTE.
explanation.definitionFit: A recurring musical or literary motif is a persistent theme.

clue.text: Surrender earnings

definitions.meaning: to give in or give way
the return or profit from an investment

explanation.surface: Giving up what one has earned.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving way and a financial return are both senses of this word.

clue.text: Piqued I tried art for a change

indicators.note: the letters of the three words are given a change of order to make a new word

explanation.surface: Someone annoyed after taking up painting as a new hobby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for a change' rearranges the letters of I TRIED ART.
explanation.definitionFit: Being piqued is being annoyed or nettled, a synonym.

clue.text: One to note in get together

parts.note: a unit is a single one of something
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: An instruction to add a musical note to a group gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: To get together is to join or combine, a synonym.

clue.text: The present that hasn't arrived yet

definitions.text: The present that hasn't arrived yet

parts.words: The present that hasn't arrived yet
parts.note: a present seems to be a gift still in the post, but it is time, and the time not yet come is what follows now

explanation.surface: A birthday gift that is still stuck in the post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'present' wants to be a gift; it is the time now, and the time that has not arrived is what lies ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: Time still to come, after the present moment, is what lies ahead of us.

clue.text: Inappropriate for learner-driver to be restricted by limited movement

indicators.note: the learner's letter is held within, as if hemmed in by the other letters
the letters of the word limited are moved about into a new order

parts.note: a learner driver displays an L-plate, so L

explanation.surface: A learner driver struggling with a car whose steering will barely turn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'movement' rearranges LIMITED into ILTIMED, and 'to be restricted by' puts L, the learner, inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something mistimed is unsuitable for the moment, so inappropriate.

clue.text: Fly from one whose lot is not a happy one

definitions.text: one whose lot is not a happy one
definitions.meaning: Gilbert and Sullivan sang that a policeman's lot is not a happy one, and old British slang names a policeman after his blue uniform

explanation.surface: Escaping from someone with a miserable life.
explanation.walkthrough: The Pirates of Penzance song says 'A policeman's lot is not a happy one'; the word is old British slang for a policeman.
explanation.definitionFit: A buzzing blowfly, and dated slang for a uniformed police officer, share one name.

clue.text: Official opportunity to turn back

parts.note: a chance is an opportunity

indicators.note: the word for turning over and over is to be read from right to left

parts.note: to roll is to turn over

explanation.surface: A bureaucrat given the chance to turn around and go home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns ROLL into LLOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A chancellor is a senior state or university official, an example of the class.

clue.text: Is he a car driver? No, this is George

definitions.text: Is he a car driver? No, this is George

parts.words: Is he a car driver? No, this is George
parts.note: the start suggests a motorist, but pilots' slang calls an aircraft's automatic flying system George

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether the man at the wheel is a chauffeur; no, he is George.
explanation.walkthrough: The device sounds like an 'auto' pilot, a car driver; airmen nicknamed the automatic pilot 'George'.
explanation.definitionFit: Aircrew slang names the automatic steering system of a plane George.

clue.text: It fixes the collar on horses

definitions.meaning: a small button-like fastener once held detachable shirt collars in place
a farm of breeding horses kept together

explanation.surface: A stable hand fastening a horse's collar.
explanation.definitionFit: A collar fastener and an establishment of breeding horses are both called by this short word.

clue.text: How to get away from a Kipling lady?

definitions.text: How to get away from a Kipling lady?

parts.words: How to get away from a Kipling lady?
parts.note: Kipling wrote of a liner as a lady, so leaving the lady means stepping off the ship

explanation.surface: Advice on escaping from a woman in a Kipling story.
explanation.walkthrough: Kipling's poem 'The Liner She's a Lady' makes the lady a ship; you leave a ship by going ashore.
explanation.definitionFit: Going ashore from a vessel is the way to leave a ship.

clue.text: In "Modern Times" the characters are no way sad

definitions.note: the present day, the times we live in

indicators.note: the letters of the phrase are its characters, to be set out afresh in a new order

explanation.surface: Chaplin's film Modern Times, whose characters are no way sad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the characters are' asks for the letters of NO WAY SAD, rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: These days, the present era, is what modern times means.

clue.text: Girlfriend good enough to eat

definitions.meaning: a romantic partner one goes out with
the sweet brown fruit of a palm tree

explanation.surface: A boyfriend telling his partner she looks good enough to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: A romantic companion for an evening and the edible palm fruit share the name.

clue.text: Mythical creatures claiming to be real

definitions.text: Mythical creatures claiming to be real

parts.words: Mythical creatures claiming to be real
parts.note: split differently, the name sounds like a past claim that they truly existed as wild dogs

explanation.surface: Legendary beasts insisting they actually exist.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as 'were wolves', the name of these shape-shifters is itself a claim of having been real animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Men who turn into wolves at full moon are creatures of folklore and myth.

clue.text: Path say leading to the altar

indicators.note: say signals the word is said aloud rather than spelt

parts.note: a bridle path is a track for horses, so path suggests bridle

explanation.surface: Describing the aisle that a couple walk up to be married.
explanation.walkthrough: A bridle path is a horse track; 'say' turns the horse's headgear into the wedding word that sounds the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to a bride and her wedding, the way to the altar.

clue.text: Newsagent's origami figure?

parts.note: a figure folded from paper would be a little lad made of paper, which is also the lad a newsagent sends out on deliveries

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper folding a newspaper into a little shape.
explanation.walkthrough: The newsagent's delivery lad is read literally as a boy made of folded paper.
explanation.definitionFit: The youngster who delivers papers for a newsagent, here imagined as folded paper.

clue.text: Deposit on a coat

parts.note: to park something is to deposit or leave it

explanation.surface: Leaving a coat in the cloakroom.
explanation.definitionFit: A hooded waterproof jacket is a kind of coat.

clue.text: Understand in depth

definitions.meaning: to work something out or grasp it
a measure of water depth equal to six feet

explanation.surface: Grasping a subject thoroughly.
explanation.definitionFit: To grasp an idea, and a six-foot unit of sea depth, share one word.

clue.text: Book a small dwelling on the water's edge

parts.note: HO is the short form of house, a dwelling shortened
the sea is the water at the edge of the land

explanation.surface: Booking a little cottage by the shore for a holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Book' looks like a verb about reserving; it is a book of the Old Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: Hosea is one of the minor prophets' books of the Old Testament.

clue.text: Notice precludes pyramid selling to some extent

indicators.note: the answer is a part of these words, found running across them

explanation.surface: A rule that bars pyramid-selling schemes, at least partly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to some extent' points to a run inside precludES PYramid.
explanation.definitionFit: To notice something is to catch sight of it, a synonym.

clue.text: Laid the law down like some papers

definitions.meaning: printed with straight lines, as writing paper often is

explanation.surface: A judge laying down the law on some documents.
explanation.definitionFit: Governed with authority, and lined like writing paper: one word covers both senses.

clue.text: A neat mass churning in the Pacific

definitions.note: the definition describes a stretch of water lying in the Pacific

indicators.note: the letters are stirred up like water churning, giving a new order

explanation.surface: A tidy body of water stirred up out in the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'churning' rearranges A NEAT MASS. It lies between Australia and New Zealand.
explanation.definitionFit: This body of water between Australia and New Zealand is part of the south-western Pacific.

clue.text: Heavy-duty battery supporting a charge

parts.note: a battery suggests an electric cell, but here it is a unit of big guns giving covering fire to troops charging

explanation.surface: A powerful electric cell holding its charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'battery' and 'charge' look electrical; a battery is also a group of heavy guns, backing up an infantry charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Big guns, organised in batteries, back up troops charging at an enemy.

clue.text: Husband in bed in rough lodging

indicators.note: the letter for husband goes inside the word for bed

parts.note: the sack is slang for bed

explanation.surface: A man lying in bed in a ramshackle dwelling.
explanation.definitionFit: A hut or hovel is crude, rough lodging.
